title: Hourly to Annual Pay: Understanding Novated Lease vs Salary Sacrifice
description: Convert hourly to annual pay with our guide. Learn about novated lease vs salary sacrifice, casual loading, super, and tax for Australian workers.
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week, your annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 1,976 hours (38 × 52).

faqs.q: What is the difference between casual loading and superannuation?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of leave entitlements. Superannuation is a separate 12% contribution paid on top of ordinary earnings (including casual loading) into a super fund. Both are calculated on the gross pay before tax.

faqs.q: How does a novated lease affect my take-home pay compared to salary sacrifice?
faqs.a: A novated lease is a type of salary sacrifice arrangement specifically for a car. Salary sacrifice generally reduces your taxable income by diverting pre-tax dollars to pay for eligible items. Both can lower your tax, but a novated lease also involves ongoing lease payments, running costs, and residual value. Use our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page to compare the net effect on your annual pay.

faqs.q: What hourly rate equals the National Minimum Wage in 2026–27?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour for permanent employees, or $33.05 per hour including 25% casual loading. This is set by the Fair Work Commission and applies to award-free employees. Award rates may be higher for specific industries or roles.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly to Annual Pay: A Complete Guide

Whether you're negotiating a salary offer or planning your budget, knowing how to convert an hourly rate to annual pay is essential. This guide uses the standard 38-hour week (full-time hours under the Fair Work Ombudsman) and explains the key factors: casual loading, superannuation, tax, and how decisions like a **novated lease vs salary sacrifice** can affect your overall package.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours × 52

The simplest way to estimate annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the multiplier is 38 × 52 = 1,976 hours per year. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (set by the Fair Work Commission from 1 July 2026), annual gross pay would be:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44

If you work fewer or more hours, adjust accordingly. This calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, and no penalty rates or allowances. It's a starting point, not a binding determination.

### Casual Loading: Adding 25% on Top

If you're a casual employee, you're entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave (annual leave, sick leave, etc.). The Fair Work Ombudsman states that casual loading is paid on top of the award or minimum rate.

**Important:** When using our [the timesheet](/), you enter your base hourly rate (the rate before casual loading). Then check the box to add 25% casual loading. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading. For example, if your base rate is $26.44, the casual rate becomes $33.05 per hour. Annual gross for a casual at that rate would be $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,336.80.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top of Your Gross

Employers must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of 12% of your ordinary earnings (from 1 July 2026). Super is paid **on top** of your gross pay, not deducted from it. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year (2026–27).

For the minimum wage example above:
- Annual gross: $52,269.44
- Super (12%): $6,272.33
- Total cost to employer: $58,541.77

Super is calculated on ordinary earnings, which include casual loading but exclude overtime. Use our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page to see how salary sacrifice arrangements can affect your super contributions.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay depends on the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy (generally 2%). The tax-free threshold is $18,200. Tax brackets:
- $0–$18,200: nil
- $18,201–$45,000: 15%
- $45,001–$135,000: 30%
- $135,001–$190,000: 37%
- $190,001+: 45%

Medicare levy reduction thresholds for singles in 2025–26 are used here (the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). For a full-time minimum wage earner ($52,269.44), estimated tax would be approximately $5,947 plus Medicare of $1,045, leaving take-home of about $45,277. This excludes HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging.

### Novated Lease vs Salary Sacrifice: What's the Difference?

When considering how to maximise your take-home pay, you might encounter two common terms: **novated lease vs salary sacrifice**. Both involve diverting pre-tax income to pay for expenses, reducing your taxable income. However, they are not identical.

- **Salary sacrifice** is an arrangement where you agree to forgo part of your salary in exchange for benefits like a car, laptop, or additional super contributions. The sacrificed amount is not subject to income tax (though fringe benefits tax may apply).
- **A novated lease** is a specific type of salary sacrifice for a vehicle. You lease a car, and the lease payments, running costs (fuel, insurance, maintenance), and sometimes the residual value are deducted from your pre-tax salary. The employer is the lessee, and you are the driver.

Both can lower your tax bill, but a novated lease involves ongoing obligations and a residual payment at the end. Salary sacrifice for other items (like super) is simpler. Use our [pay guides](/blog) to compare how each affects your annual net income.

### Using the Timesheet and Reference Tables

Our [the timesheet]() lets you enter your base hourly rate and toggle casual loading. It then calculates annual gross, fortnightly pay, estimated tax, super, and take-home. The [reference tables](/data) provide award rates, industry averages, and the National Minimum Wage.

Remember: the Australian Bureau of Statistics' Average Weekly Earnings (May 2026) show full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week. That is an **average**, not a median for any specific job. Your actual pay may differ based on your award, enterprise agreement, or individual contract.

### Fortnightly Pay: A Handy Check

Many employers pay fortnightly. To estimate your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a full-time minimum wage earner:
- Weekly: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.72
- Fortnightly: $1,004.72 × 2 = $2,009.44

Super and tax are calculated on the annual amount, but fortnightly deductions help with budgeting.

### Final Notes

This guide provides estimates only. Always check your specific award or agreement via the Fair Work Ombudsman. For tax advice, consult the Australian Taxation Office or a registered tax agent. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page has the latest rates, and [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) shows net figures after tax and Medicare.

Whether you're comparing a **novated lease vs salary sacrifice** or just converting your hourly rate, understanding these components ensures you make informed decisions about your pay package.
